problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Every component f_i is convex on E; the regularizer r is strongly convex, so F(x)=n⁻¹∑ᵢf_i(x)+r(x) is convex.

problem_class.label: strongly_convex
problem_class.details: The regularizer r is μ-strongly convex on all of E, with μ>0; consequently the composite objective is μ-strongly convex.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositeFiniteSumStronglyConvex.lean: spec.valid and spec.admissible, StrongConvexOn univ p.μ inst.regularizer.

problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: A differentiable smooth finite-sum term is added to a real-valued regularizer whose exact proximal minimizers are available; no smoothness of the regularizer is required.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: The smooth term is the average of n≥1 convex components, each with an L-Lipschitz gradient, where L>0.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: A query selects any index i and point x and returns exactly ∇f_i(x), independently of the call index and oracle seed. There is no oracle noise or restriction to random index selection.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: For any a>0 and z,g∈E, the oracle returns an exact global minimizer of ‖v−z‖²/(2a)+⟪g,v−z⟫+r(v). Each proximal query counts as one oracle call, as does each component-gradient query.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositeFiniteSumStronglyConvex.lean: Query.prox and spec.admissible proximal conditions; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is an arbitrary complete real inner-product space with a measurable-space structure; finite dimensionality is not assumed. All parameters E,n,L,μ,Δ,ε,x0 are public, with n≥1, L>0, μ>0, Δ≥0, ε>0. The components, regularizer, and proximal map are hidden instance data. A minimizer x* exists with F(x0)−F(x*)≤Δ. Smoothness is componentwise rather than merely average smoothness.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositeFiniteSumStronglyConvex.lean: Params, Instance, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is a measurable E-valued random point. For some global minimizer x*, its objective gap is integrable and has integral at most ε; no distance or gradient-norm criterion is imposed.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The guarantee is E[F(output)−F(x*)]≤ε under the product of algorithm and oracle seed laws. The oracle budget is fixed and holds for every seed; accuracy is required only in expectation.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is the standard strongly convex composite finite-sum minimization formulation with exact component gradients, exact proximal access, known parameters, and expected objective-gap accuracy, stated over a real Hilbert space.
